bib.title: Emergent Analogical Reasoning in Large Language Models

read.skipped: Supplementary example transcripts (S4, S5 chat logs) skimmed, not read line by line; reference list skimmed.

question: Can a large language model solve analogy problems zero-shot at human level?
hypothesis: LLMs trained only on next-token prediction may acquire an emergent capacity for zero-shot analogical reasoning.
contributions: Digit Matrices, a text-based Raven-style problem set guaranteed novel to humans and models
new letter-string problem set and new human data for four task families
direct GPT-3 vs human comparison with error-pattern analysis
qualitative analogical problem solving and preliminary GPT-4 story analogy test

method.summary: Zero-shot evaluation of text-davinci-003 (and, in the supplement, davinci, code-davinci-002, text-davinci-002) on four analogy task families, compared with new human data from UCLA undergraduates: Digit Matrices (new text Raven-style task), letter-string analogies, four-term verbal analogies, story analogies; plus qualitative analogical problem solving. A preliminary GPT-4 run covers story analogies only.

datasets.name: Digit Matrices (new)
datasets.size: 100 instances per subtype generated; 32 subtypes in exp 1 (6 one-rule, 6 two-rule, 10 three-rule, 10 logic), 42 in exp 2 (adds 4- and 5-rule); GPT-3 gets 40 instances per subtype
datasets.source: authors; rules follow Matzen et al. 2010; 8 answer choices (7 procedural distractors)
datasets.preprocessing: 3x3 grid, cells in brackets, digits; logic problems aligned or permuted

datasets.name: Letter string analogies (new)
datasets.size: 600 problems generated at each generalization level (zero to three) (100 per type for 0 and 1); GPT-3 evaluated on 300 each (50 per type); 50 real-world-concept problems per transformation type (4 types); humans 28 problems each

datasets.name: SAT analogies (Turney et al.)
datasets.source: not public; human estimate from Turney and Littman 2005

datasets.name: Gentner et al. 1993 story analogies
datasets.size: 18 source stories x 4 targets; 72 GPT comparisons
datasets.source: Gentner et al. 1993 Exp 2; via Ichien et al. 2020 inventory

datasets.name: Radiation / gumball analogical problem solving
datasets.source: Gick and Holyoak 1980; Holyoak et al. 1984; Holyoak and Koh 1987

other.scope: story analogies only, via ChatGPT web interface, no API access

inference.decoding: greedy (temperature 0); multiple-choice via average log probability of choice tokens (Digit Matrices) or log prob of final term (verbal analogies)
inference.max_tokens: 10 Digit Matrices, 40 letter strings, 10 verbal analogies, 256 story analogies and problem solving
inference.samples: one deterministic completion per item; Digit Matrices exp 2 ordering: 20 runs; story analogies 72 comparisons, context cleared each time
inference.prompting: Digit Matrices: no prompt or examples; letter strings: 'Let's try to complete the pattern:' ; verbal analogies: A:B::C:D colon notation with earlier problems and choices appended to context; story analogies: fixed template

parameters.other_params: all other OpenAI API parameters left at defaults
parameters.truncation: generations truncated at closing bracket (period for sentence format)
parameters.scoring_generative: logic problems correct if right digit set in any order; transformation problems need right digits in right order

other.context_carryover: verbal analogies and Digit Matrices exp 2 append each problem and chosen answer to prompt; oldest problems deleted when exceeding 4096 tokens

metrics.name: accuracy (generative)
metrics.definition: exact match to correct answer as per scoring rule

metrics.name: accuracy (multiple-choice)
metrics.definition: choice with highest average log probability

baselines: UCLA undergraduates (N=40, 57, 54, 47), Yale N=20, Wayne State N=241, MTurk, SAT students estimate
eval.protocol: Trial-level logistic regression (R 4.2.2), correlations over subtypes, binomial test for GPT-3 and one-sample t-test for humans on story analogies assuming 50% chance; no seeds (temp 0).

availability.data: same GitHub repo (Digit Matrices, letter strings, UCLA VAT, human data); other sets via AnalogyInventory.zip

results.claim: GPT-3 beat human participants on generative Digit Matrices (odds ratio of correct for GPT-3 vs humans).
results.setup: text-davinci-003, zero-shot, 40 instances x 32 subtypes vs N=40 UCLA undergraduates, logistic regression, generative answers

results.claim: GPT-3 beat humans on multiple-choice Digit Matrices (8 choices, mean log-prob scoring).
results.setup: text-davinci-003 zero-shot, 8 answer choices, vs N=40 humans

results.claim: GPT-3 pattern of subtype accuracy correlates modestly with humans on Digit Matrices.
results.setup: accuracy across 32 problem subtypes, GPT-3 vs humans

results.claim: GPT-3 beat humans on letter-string analogies overall.
results.setup: text-davinci-003, temperature 0, prompt 'Let's try to complete the pattern:', vs N=57 humans, generative

results.claim: GPT-3 and humans show similar error patterns across letter-string subtypes.
results.setup: 41 subtypes with >=5 trials each from GPT-3 and humans

results.claim: Letter-string accuracy falls with number of generalizations in GPT-3 (stronger than humans).
Without the prompt, GPT-3 letter-string correlation with human pattern drops but remains.
results.note: Sentence format r = 0.76. Performance fell with format change but stayed within one SD of humans.

results.claim: Semantic distance hurts GPT-3 on Jones et al. verbal analogies as in humans.
results.setup: Jones et al. 120 problems, near vs far, N=241 humans; log-prob choice of D
results.quote: effect of semantic distance for GPT-3: OR = 3.24, p = 0.0165
results.note: Direction of OR as printed in paper (OR>1 as stated for 'effect of semantic distance').

results.claim: On story analogies GPT-3 is worse than humans overall.
results.setup: 72 comparisons (18 stories x near/far x 2 orders), forced choice, vs N=54 humans

results.claim: GPT-3 is above chance in near analogy but not in far analogy story comparisons.
15 of 54 students picked the analogous story on every trial.
results.quote: a significant number of participants (15/54) selected the analogous story on every trial

results.claim: GPT-3 failed to use story analogy for gumball physical task though could map the analogy; authors attribute to weak physical reasoning.
results.setup: Qualitative, OpenAI playground, uncurated single sessions
results.quote: its lack of physical reasoning skills

results.claim: Qualitative: GPT-3 gave the convergence solution to the radiation problem only after the analogous general story, and lost it with distractor stories unless prompted to consider earlier stories.
results.setup: Qualitative, single sessions, Gick and Holyoak paradigm

results.claim: Preliminary: GPT-4 nearly perfect on near analogy story comparisons and more robust on far.
results.setup: Same 72 problems via ChatGPT web interface; only story analogies tested
results.quote: displaying nearly perfect performance in the near analogy condition

limits: Only text-davinci-003 in the main text; GPT-4 tested on story analogies only for lack of API access.
Digit Matrices are pseudo-symbolic, not visual; no test of perception.
Tests limited to a local context: no long-term retrieval of analogs, GPT-3 forgets once the context is cleared.
Poor on physical reasoning (gumball transfer) and far story analogies.
Format sensitivity: letter-string accuracy fell with no prompt or sentence format.
Test-set contamination checked only by prompting for memorisation (Supp S3), not ruled out for letter strings, VAT, SAT, radiation problem.
Per-condition accuracies are given only in figures, not text; humans are college students on online tasks; the mechanism is not identified.
Later work disputes the emergent-reasoning reading (not in this paper).
